excerpt: Podium is a Utah company selling an AI Employee, messaging, reviews and payments to local businesses such as car dealerships and home services. Pricing is by quote.
content:
Podium is a Utah software company for local businesses. It started with tools for collecting online reviews and talking to customers by text, then added payments; TechCrunch reported in 2020 that Podium let its customers take payments inside text conversations, with processing through Stripe. Today the company leads with what it calls an AI Employee: an assistant that answers calls, texts and web chats around the clock, qualifies leads, books appointments and re-engages past customers. Its website offers industry versions for auto dealerships, home services, aesthetics and retail, and says more than 60,000 businesses use Podium.

Eric Rea is Podium's CEO. TechCrunch reported in March 2020 that 43,000 businesses used Podium at the time.

Funding

Podium raised $125 million at a valuation of about $1.5 billion in April 2020, and on 15 November 2021 TechCrunch reported a $201 million round that valued the company at $3 billion post-money. Rea told Bloomberg then that Podium had well over $100 million in annual recurring revenue.

Pricing

Podium does not publish prices. Its pricing page says plans are built around each business's needs and asks you to talk to sales; the AI Employee can be added to any plan, and onboarding, phone and chat support and customer success managers are included in every plan.

Who it suits

Podium suits local businesses that live on inbound leads and appointments, such as car dealers, home service companies, med spas and retailers, and that struggle to answer every call and message quickly. Online-only businesses or companies that sell mainly to other businesses may find it less relevant.

We have not tested Podium. This page is based on Podium's website and pricing page (checked 15 October 2026) and TechCrunch reporting from 2020 and 2021.
